title: GPS Coordinates Linked to Device Identity
description: The device's unique identifier (e.g., IMEI, MAC address, or device ID) is transmitted to the backend, allowing the backend to link the GPS data to a specific individual.
assumptions: The device ID is unique and globally or locally identifiable.

title: GPS Coordinates Transmitted in Transit
description: The live GPS coordinates are transmitted over the network, potentially exposing the data to interception or metadata leakage.
assumptions: Network transmission is not encrypted or secured.

title: Sensitive Data Type Disclosed
description: The backend processes GPS coordinates, which are considered highly sensitive personal data, without strict functional necessity.
assumptions: GPS coordinates are not strictly required for the core functionality of the Mobile App Backend.

title: Linking via Unique Identifier
description: The mobile app backend writes location pings to the Location History Store. This action links the data subject (identified by the app's unique identifier) to the data store using that identifier.
assumptions: The app uses a unique identifier to identify the user.

title: Data Type Sensitivity
description: The Location History Store stores location data. Location data is considered highly sensitive personal data and should only be collected and processed when strictly required.
assumptions: Location data is classified as sensitive personal data.

title: Linking via Unique Identifier
description: The Family Account Store (DS2) contains unique identifiers (e.g., user IDs, email addresses) that are used to link data to specific individuals. When the Geofencing Engine reads this data, it can identify the data subjects associated with the stored records, enabling the engine to link geofencing rules to specific individuals.
assumptions: The Family Account Store contains identifiable personal data.

title: Linking via Quasi-identifier
description: The data flow DF4 carries metadata about the parties involved in the data exchange (e.g., the specific user accounts being accessed). This metadata can be used to link the data flow to specific individuals, potentially identifying the data subjects associated with the stored account data.
assumptions: The data flow carries metadata about the parties involved.

title: Observed Communications
description: The Geofencing & Alert Engine (P2) processes the data from the Family Account Store. The act of processing and analyzing the stored account data (e.g., checking if a user is in a specific zone) constitutes observed communications, as the system's processing of the data is observable.
assumptions: The Geofencing Engine processes the data from the Family Account Store.

title: Linking via Unique Identifier
description: The Geofencing Engine (P2) shares arrival/departure notifications with the parent (EE1) using a unique identifier (e.g., a unique ID for the child entity or a unique ID for the zone). This allows the parent to link the notification to a specific individual or entity, enabling identification.
assumptions: The notification contains a unique identifier that is globally or locally unique.

title: Processing of Identified Information
description: The Geofencing Engine (P2) processes the arrival/departure notification, which contains identified information (e.g., a unique identifier for the child entity or zone). The system requests and processes this data to perform the geofencing logic.
assumptions: The notification contains identifiable information.

title: Data Type Sensitivity
description: The Geofencing Engine (P2) processes personal data (the arrival/departure notification) of a more fine-grained level of granularity than functionally needed for the basic geofencing logic. The notification likely contains specific personal data attributes (e.g., exact location coordinates, precise timestamps) that are not strictly required for the core function of pushing a generic 'arrival' or 'departure' flag.
assumptions: The notification contains detailed personal data beyond what is functionally required.

title: Unlawful Processing of Personal Data
description: The Geofencing Engine (P2) processes personal data (the arrival/departure notification) in a way that may not be lawful. For example, if the notification contains sensitive personal data (e.g., exact location coordinates) and the processing is not justified by a valid legal ground (e.g., consent, legal obligation), this constitutes unlawful processing.
assumptions: The processing of the notification's personal data does not have a valid legal basis.

title: Unawareness of Processing
description: The Geofencing Engine (P2) processes personal data (the arrival/departure notification) without the data subject (the child entity) being aware of this processing. The child entity does not know that its arrival/departure notification is being collected, processed, or stored by the parent.
assumptions: The child entity is unaware that its notification is being processed by the parent.

title: Lack of Data Subject Control
description: The Geofencing Engine (P2) lacks control over how the arrival/departure notification is processed. The child entity cannot choose or customize which, how, or how long its notification is processed by the parent.
assumptions: The child entity has no control over the processing of its notification.

title: Lack of Control in Accessing Personal Data
description: The Geofencing Engine (P2) lacks control in accessing the personal data (the arrival/departure notification) that is being processed. The child entity cannot access or modify the notification data.
assumptions: The child entity cannot access the notification data.

title: Lack of Control in Rectifying Incorrect Data
description: The Geofencing Engine (P2) lacks control in rectifying incorrect data or removing personal data that is no longer relevant. If the notification contains incorrect data or becomes obsolete, the child entity cannot request correction or erasure.
assumptions: The child entity cannot request correction or erasure of its notification data.

title: Invalid Consent
description: The Geofencing Engine (P2) relies on invalid consent for the processing of the arrival/departure notification. The consent obtained by the child entity may not be valid, or the consent is not specific enough to cover the processing of the notification.
assumptions: The consent for processing the notification is invalid or insufficient.

title: Violation of Data Minimization Principle
description: The Geofencing Engine (P2) processes more personal data (the arrival/departure notification) than is actually needed. The notification likely contains more data than is strictly required for the basic geofencing function (e.g., it might contain unnecessary metadata or attributes).
assumptions: The notification contains more data than functionally required.

title: Lawfulness Problems Not Related to Consent
description: The Geofencing Engine (P2) processes personal data (the arrival/departure notification) in a way that violates lawfulness requirements not related to consent. For example, if the notification contains sensitive personal data (e.g., exact location) and the processing is not justified by a valid legal ground other than consent, this is a lawfulness problem.

title: Invalid Consent

assumptions: The consent for processing the notification is invalid or insufficient.

title: Violation of Storage Limitation Principle
description: The Geofencing Engine (P2) stores personal data (the arrival/departure notification) longer than functionally needed. The notification is likely kept in storage for a longer duration than required for the geofencing function.
assumptions: The notification is stored longer than functionally needed.

title: Generic Regulatory Noncompliance
description: The Geofencing Engine (P2) may violate generic regulatory noncompliance principles. For example, if the processing of the notification does not meet general data protection principles (e.g., transparency, accountability) without being specific to a particular legal regime.
assumptions: The processing of the notification does not meet general data protection principles.

title: Insufficient Cybersecurity Risk Management
description: The Geofencing Engine (P2) may lack proper cybersecurity risk management with specific attention to the interplay with privacy risks. The notification is shared with a parent entity, which may introduce additional security risks that are not adequately managed.
assumptions: The Geofencing Engine does not adequately manage cybersecurity risks related to sharing the notification.

title: Non-compliance with Privacy Standards and Best Practices
description: The Geofencing Engine (P2) may be non-compliant with privacy standards and best practices. For example, if the notification is shared with a parent entity without proper safeguards, or if the sharing amplifies the potential risk of data exposure.

If the data elements are perceived as highly sensitive (e.g., personal data about an individual's location, family relationships, or private account details), the sharing of this data may be considered excessive. description: The backend process shares account, child profile, and geofence zone data with the Family Account & Permissions Store. If the processing of this data does not rely on valid consent or a lawful ground, it may constitute a threat of Non-compliance (Nc). description: The mobile app backend (P1) processes the parent's request to view the child's location. This involves observing and processing observed communications (the request and the data flow) to retrieve and display the location information.

This linking through a unique identifier creates a privacy risk as the data subject's identity can be inferred or directly identified.

assumptions: The secondary guardian is a dynamic party that may change frequently.

description: The secondary guardian receives the live location data and observes the communication of this data, which allows them to detect and track the user's movements.

This linking through unique identifiers creates a privacy risk as the data subject's identity can be reconstructed from the shared data.

This data likely contains identifiers (e.g., unique IDs, device IDs, or session tokens) that directly identify the data subject, allowing the partner to link the data to specific individuals.

description: The backend shares aggregated usage and engagement analytics with the advertising/analytics partner. This data is highly sensitive personal data (e.g., usage patterns, engagement metrics) that should be collected and processed only when strictly required. Sharing this data with a third party for advertising purposes may be excessive and unnecessary.

title: Excessive Volume
description: The backend shares aggregated usage and engagement analytics with the advertising/analytics partner. This data involves a large volume of personal data (usage patterns, engagement metrics) that is processed beyond what is functionally needed for the app's free tier.
assumptions: The volume of personal data shared is excessive.

assumptions: The data is propagated to a third party where it is not functionally needed.

assumptions: The set of parties with whom the data is shared is known and static.

title: Availability/Accessibility of Data
description: The backend shares aggregated usage and engagement analytics with the advertising/analytics partner. This data is published or broadcasted by the system to a third party, which greatly amplifies the potential risk of data exposure.
assumptions: The data is published or broadcasted to a third party.

title: Unawareness of Processing
description: The backend shares aggregated usage and engagement analytics with the advertising/analytics partner. The data subject may not be aware that their usage and engagement data is being shared with a third party for advertising purposes.

description: The backend shares aggregated usage and engagement analytics with the advertising/analytics partner. The data subject may not have control over how their usage and engagement data is processed or shared with the advertising/analytics partner.

description: The backend shares aggregated usage and engagement analytics with the advertising/analytics partner. This data is not processed in a lawful way, as the sharing for advertising purposes may not have a valid legal ground (e.g., consent, legitimate interest) and may violate privacy standards.

title: Linking via Unique Identifier
description: The Child (ExternalEntity) sends a manual check-in / SOS message with their current location to the parent. This message contains a unique identifier (e.g., a unique ID for the Child or a unique location coordinate) that allows the parent to link the message to a specific individual. This creates a threat where the parent can identify the data subject solely from the message content.
assumptions: The message includes a unique identifier for the Child.

title: Data Type Sensitivity
description: The Child sends a message containing their current location. Location data is considered highly sensitive personal data. The threat arises because this sensitive data is being transmitted, potentially exposing the individual's precise location to the parent, which may be considered excessive or unnecessary for the purpose of a simple check-in.
assumptions: Location data is considered highly sensitive personal data.

title: Unawareness of Processing
description: The Child (ExternalEntity) is unaware that their current location is being transmitted to the parent. The threat arises because the data subject is not aware that their personal data (location) is being collected, processed, or disclosed by the parent.
assumptions: The Child is unaware that their location is being transmitted.

title: Lawfulness Problems Not Related to Consent
description: The Child sends a manual check-in / SOS message with their current location. The threat arises because the processing of this data (location) may not be lawful. For example, if the parent does not have a valid legal basis (e.g., consent, legal obligation) to process the location data, or if the processing is automated in a way that violates privacy standards, this constitutes a non-compliance threat.
assumptions: The parent's processing of the location data may not be lawful.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the parent has a valid legal basis for processing location data.

title: Attributable Data Evidence
description: The Child sends a message with their current location. This message can be attributed to the Child (the data subject) because it contains data that is unique to them (e.g., their location). This creates a threat where the parent can attribute the message to the Child, potentially preventing the Child from denying certain claims about the message's origin or content.
assumptions: The message content is unique to the Child.

title: Observed Communications
description: The Child sends a message with their current location to the parent. This constitutes observed communications, where the parent observes the transmission of the message. The threat arises because the parent can detect the existence of the message and the data contained within it.
assumptions: The parent observes the transmission of the message.
